texts: Mire-essence is a thick dark oil.
Mire-essence burns with a pale silver flame.
The pale silver flame of mire-essence is mist-light.
There is no substitute for mire-essence.
Keepers make mire-essence from silken threads and sea-water.
Mire-essence comes from the copper cauldrons.

fields.sentence: Mire-essence is a thick dark oil.

review.notes: Kind subject correctly takes Inheritance, the mire_essence genus is emitted with no 'mire' modifier atom (noun modifier), and the stacked descriptive adjectives 'thick dark' stay unfused as separate property atoms per the incidental-description rule. The 0.99/0.9 split (taxonomic 'is an oil' vs contingent thick/dark) is a defensible application of the definitional-vs-empirical dial.

q1_issues.issue: (Member sk_smell_1 metallic) predicates the adjective of the smelling eventuality itself, a shape the instruction set never licenses — an event witness carries a class, role and status atoms, while an adjective attaches to an entity or to a reified adjective-state witness whose own class IS the adjective.
This conjunct carries (STV 0.9 0.9) while the sibling atoms of the same event bundle (statements 1, 2, 4) carry 0.99, so one claim is graded two ways with no stated reason.

The bare mass kind symbol mire_essence fills an individual's Experiencer slot in a flat unmarked event; a habitual/characteristic clause with a bare kind subject is the verbal-generic Implication-rule form under 'Quantifiers, generics & scope', not a single asserted event.

q2_gaps: copular / linking perception verb with a predicative adjective — 'X smells / tastes / sounds / looks ADJ' — where the subject is the stimulus rather than a perceiver: 'Two kinds of clause' forces it to the verbal/event route, but the adjectival complement then has no licensed slot (it is not Manner, not a resultative, not a depictive on the subject, and Perception reports covers only a perceiver subject with an eventive or entity complement)

a degree adverb downtoning a predicative adjective under such a verb ('faintly metallic') — Degree's bearer slot is defined for an entity, and no rule says whether the bearer is the subject or the reified state
review.notes: The compound genus (Inheritance mire_essence essence) with the noun modifier left unexposed is correct. The parse does at least avoid asserting the essence IS metallic, but it does so with an unlicensed shape rather than by recording the gap.

issues.reason: Member takes an individual plus a class or property and sk_smell_1 is a minted witness, so the atom is well-typed and true of the sentence's content (what the text calls metallic is the smell, not the essence -- the parse correctly avoids the false (Inheritance mire_essence metallic)); objecting to the shape is objecting to graceful improvisation inside the very gap the reviewer files.

No rule requires one clause's atoms to share a truth value -- the instruction set routinely mixes them (epistemic status at 0.9 beside 0.99 role atoms, a 0.99 QuantifierPhrase companion beside a 0.9 rule) -- and 0.9/0.9 is the dial's licensed value for the one contingent kind-level claim in the sentence, the class, role and Degree atoms keeping the structural default.

Quantifiers, generics & scope states that a non-modal verbal generic over a kind becomes an Implication rule with a Skolem-function event ('Birds fly'), and the bare-kind filler is reserved for non-specific OBJECTS ('pays tax'), so putting mire_essence in the Experiencer slot of a flat event predicates the eventuality of the kind itself instead of distributing it to instances.

gaps_confirmed: linking / perception verb with a predicative adjective ('X smells / tastes / looks ADJ') where the subject is the stimulus, not a perceiver: Two kinds of clause routes it to the verbal event form, but the adjectival complement then has no licensed slot (not Manner, not a resultative, not a depictive of the subject, and Perception reports covers only perceiver subjects)

a degree adverb downtoning that predicative adjective ('faintly metallic'): every stated Degree example gives the bearer slot an entity, and nothing says whether the bearer is the subject or a reified state
new_gaps: the two doctrines collide here: even in the mandated verbal-generic Implication form, the conclusion bundle has slots only for the event class, roles and status, so the predicative adjective still has nowhere to go -- a licensed form would need either an adjective slot on the Skolem event or a kind-level 'smells ADJ' property head
adjudication.defect_summary: For the confirmed issue the compliant form is the distributing rule (Implication (Member $x mire_essence) (And (Member (sk_smell $x) smell) (Experiencer (sk_smell $x) $x) ...)) at STV 0.9 0.9 instead of the flat event with the kind in the Experiencer slot; but no licensed slot exists for 'metallic' inside that conclusion either, so the sentence's content has no fully compliant form and that half is filed as a gap.
adjudication.notes: The compound genus (Inheritance mire_essence essence) with the noun modifier 'mire' left unexposed is correct, as is the lemma-preserving Degree level 'faintly' for a downtoner. The defect is the generic form, not the improvised adjective attachment.

q1_issues.issue: (Inheritance dark_green_black green) hands 'green' to anything of that blended colour, a claim 'dark green-black' does not make, and the Compound-concepts decomposition rules cover compound kinds/actions/nominalizations while adjective compounds are told to stay opaque.

q2_gaps: multi-word / blended colour adjective ('dark green-black'): the instruction set parks adjective compounds as opaque and gives no decomposition shape for one, nor any treatment of a shade modifier like 'dark' (which is not in the Degree intensifier inventory)
review.notes: The kind subject, Inheritance relation, the mire_essence genus with the noun modifier left unexposed, and the 0.9/0.9 empirical-generic TV all follow the instruction set; only the three-way genus split of the colour term goes beyond it.

issues.reason: The decomposition shapes are defined only for compound actions, phrasal verbs, modifier_noun compound kinds and agent-nominalizations, with adjective compounds explicitly parked ("Leave opaque for now (don't force): adjective / condition compounds"), and the split over-asserts: with (Inheritance mire_essence dark_green_black) it derives that mire-essence is green — and, by the sibling atom, black — neither of which "dark green-black" (one blended shade) states.

gaps_confirmed: No decomposition shape (and no shade-modifier treatment — "dark" is not a Degree intensifier) is legislated for a multi-word / blended colour adjective such as "dark green-black"; the section that would cover it tells you to leave adjective compounds opaque.
adjudication.defect_summary: The compliant form keeps dark_green_black as one OPAQUE property symbol — (: mire_color (Inheritance mire_essence dark_green_black) (STV 0.9 0.9)) beside (: mire_genus (Inheritance mire_essence essence) (STV 1.0 0.99)) — with none of the three (Inheritance dark_green_black dark|green|black) atoms.
adjudication.notes: The reviewer indexed only the `green` atom, but the same unlicensed split produces `dark` and `black`, and `black` is the most clearly false of the three. Everything else — the kind subject on Inheritance, the mire_essence genus with the noun modifier unexposed, and the 0.9/0.9 empirical dial — is right.

fields.sentence: Mire-essence burns with a pale silver flame.
parse: (: me_burn_rule (Implication (Member $x mire_essence) (And (Member (sk_burn $x) burn) (Patient (sk_burn $x) $x) (Instrument (sk_burn $x) (sk_flame $x)) (Member (sk_flame $x) flame) (Member (sk_flame $x) pale) (Member (sk_flame $x) silver))) (STV 0.9 0.9))

q2_gaps: manner-descriptive "with"-PP on an event ("burns with a pale silver flame") — the with-phrase test offers only CoAgent (an animate participant) or Instrument (the means it is performed by), and Manner is restricted to how-adverbs, so a with-PP that describes the manner rather than naming a means has no clean slot
review.notes: The rule route for the mass generic, 0.9/0.9 empirical strength with no QuantifierPhrase, Patient for the burn undergoer, the mire_essence head genus without the noun-modifier genus, and the $x-dependent Skolem flame witness all follow doctrine. Instrument is the nearest licensed slot for "with a pale silver flame", but it reads the flame as the means the burning is performed by rather than as its appearance.

fields.sentence: The pale silver flame of mire-essence is mist-light.

review.notes: "Of mire-essence" takes the opaque Possession catch-all, correct because "flame" is a relational/non-deverbal noun with no underlying verb for the nominalization-object Of route, and the definite singular keeps the individual-witness default. "Pale silver" splits into two independent property atoms, the only route the colour/incidental-description fusion bar leaves open.

fields.sentence: There is no substitute for mire-essence.

q2_gaps: a NEGATED existential "there is no N (for X)": the instruction set gives the positive "there is a X" witness form, the copular "no N is P" strength-0 `Inheritance` form, and the negated-event bundle, but no form for denying existence -- the witness-bundle route taken here denies one anonymous witness rather than every substitute, so the universal force of "no" is lost and a later `sk_substitute_2` would not be contradicted

the `no`-quantifier's mandatory `(QuantifierPhrase <subject> <predicate> "no")` companion has no slot to fill in an existence denial: there is no predicate argument and no quantified range, and the instruction set's own caveat (the companion "only ever restates a range the rule itself quantifies") then bars emitting one -- the two rules conflict for this construction
review.notes: Within the licensed inventory the encoding is right: the indefinite witness and its typing stay inside the strength-0 `(And ...)` while the definitional `mire_essence` genus projects to top level, and `(For sk_substitute_1 mire_essence)` is the licensed entity-attached argument preposition on a noun complement (*Complements of nouns and adjectives*), not a coined head. The gap is that the nearest licensed shape is strictly weaker than the sentence.

fields.sentence: Keepers make mire-essence from silken threads and sea-water.
parse: (: keepers_make (Implication (Member $x keeper) (And (Member (sk_make $x) make) (Agent (sk_make $x) $x) (Patient (sk_make $x) mire_essence) (Source (sk_make $x) silken_thread) (Source (sk_make $x) sea_water))) (STV 0.9 0.9))

q2_gaps: coordinated NPs filling ONE oblique role ('make X from A and B', where A and B are co-ingredients of a single event) — the stated default for coordinated NPs is distributive replication of the whole predication, which would wrongly mint two making events, and the collective carve-out is restricted to reciprocal/aggregate predicates and 'together/jointly'; nothing licenses the (correct) two-Source-atoms-on-one-event form the parse uses
review.notes: Decomposition is exactly right — genus for all three compounds, the material ADJECTIVE 'silken' exposed as a modifier genus while the noun modifiers 'mire' and 'sea' are not; bare-generic 0.9/0.9 with no QuantifierPhrase and no tense atom is correct. Sentence-initial 'Keepers' has no definite article, so the common-noun reading (not a Name-only plural label) is the right one.

fields.sentence: Mire-essence comes from the copper cauldrons.

q1_issues.issue: The bare mass-kind subject 'Mire-essence' is used as a role filler in a single flat event, but a verbal generic over a kind is prescribed as an Implication rule over instances, and the bare class symbol is reserved for non-specific OBJECTS, not for a generic subject.

q2_gaps: bare MASS-noun generic subject: the verbal-generic rule form ranges over (Member $x <kind>) instances, which is undefined for a substance kind, and the bare-plural-episodic fallback (a group witness) has no mass counterpart
review.notes: The definite plural 'the copper cauldrons' correctly becomes a group witness with the fused material classifier in the kind slot plus its genus, and 'from' correctly takes the Source oblique; as a kind-level claim the content would also take empirical 0.9 confidence rather than 0.99.

issues.reason: *Quantifiers, generics & scope* prescribes a distributing Implication rule with a per-instance Skolem event for a non-modal verbal generic over a kind — the 'Foxes rarely cross the causeway' example is exactly this shape, a bare-kind subject with a definite object held as a constant in the conclusion — and the bare class symbol is licensed as a role filler only for non-specific / generic OBJECTS, so the flat event with mire_essence in Theme takes a form the instruction set does not license and never distributes to any portion of the substance.

gaps_confirmed: The generics machinery never states what a MASS / substance kind ranges over in the rule premise: the mass-partitive shape (Member <portion> <mass>) makes (Member $x mire_essence) workable, but that licence is nowhere stated, and the bare-plural-episodic fallback (a group witness) has no mass counterpart.
adjudication.defect_summary: The compliant form is the distributing rule (Implication (Member $x mire_essence) (And (Member (sk_come $x) come) (Theme (sk_come $x) $x) (Source (sk_come $x) sk_cauldron_1))) at (STV 0.9 0.9) — the 'Foxes rarely cross the causeway' shape, with the definite group kept as a constant in the conclusion — beside the top-level genus and GroupOf atoms.
adjudication.notes: The group witness for the definite plural, the fused material classifier with its head genus and the modifier noun left unexposed, and Source for 'from' are all correct; as a kind-level claim the content should also carry the empirical confidence 0.9 rather than 0.99.
